entities.name: Ivan Bezpaly
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ivan Bezpaly, a pivotal figure during the turbulent period of Ukrainian history known as the Ruin, was a Cossack colonel of the Uman Regiment and a staunch leader of the pro-Russian faction in Eastern Ukraine. His significance lies in his brief but consequential tenure as acting Hetman of Ukraine, from November 1658 to October 1659, a period that saw the deepening of Muscovite influence and the fragmentation of the Cossack Hetmanate. Bezpaly's actions were instrumental in cementing the loyalty of the Left-Bank Cossacks to the Tsardom of Russia, directly opposing the pro-Polish policies of Hetman Ivan Vyhovsky and thereby contributing to the geopolitical division of Ukraine.

Elected by a limited group of Left-Bank Ukraine Cossacks following the defeat of Hetman Vyhovsky at the Battle of Konotop in July 1659, Bezpaly's hetmanship was a direct result of Muscovite intervention and support. He formally pledged allegiance to Tsar Aleksey Mikhailovich, solidifying the Russian presence east of the Dnieper River. His administration, though short-lived, was marked by efforts to stabilize the Left-Bank under Russian suzerainty and to counter the remaining influence of Vyhovsky and his Polish-aligned supporters, particularly after Vyhovsky's deposition in October 1659 and the subsequent election of Yurii Khmelnytsky under Muscovite terms.

Bezpaly's role contributed significantly to the eventual political and territorial division of Ukraine along the Dnieper, a schism formally recognized by the Truce of Andrusovo in 1667 and the Eternal Peace of 1686. His leadership helped establish the precedent of Muscovite-backed hetmans on the Left-Bank, setting the stage for the progressive erosion of Cossack autonomy and the eventual incorporation of Left-Bank Ukraine into the Russian Empire. He died in 1718, having witnessed the long-term consequences of the choices made during his active political life.
